brief: Alban, the first British martyr, was beheaded on the orders of the Roman governor of Verulamium for concealing a Christian priest and then converting to the Christian faith. When soldiers came to arrest the priest, Alban surrendered himself in the priest’s place. This is traditionally dated in 304 during the empire-wide persecution of Christians, but it may have been earlier. St Alban’s Abbey is near the site of Alban’s burial, and the cult of St Alban was popular in Britain for a long time.
